Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Ezra: Much of Ezra, the account of the return from Babylonian exile, is written in Aramaic, including copies of letters from Persian kings.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Nehemiah: A cupbearer to the Persian king, Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem and, by the book's account, rebuilt its broken walls in just 52 days.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Esther: This book never once names God. It explains the origin of Purim, the festival still celebrated with costumes and noisy rattles.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Job: The story of a blameless man who loses everything wrestles with why good people suffer; Job's patience is proverbial, though he often protests angrily.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Ecclesiastes: Its famous 'a time to be born, and a time to die' passage became the 1960s hit 'Turn! Turn! Turn!' by Pete Seeger and The Byrds.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Song of Solomon: Rabbi Akiva called this book of love poetry the 'holy of holies' of Scripture, and it is read aloud in many Jewish communities at Passover.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Jeremiah: Called the 'weeping prophet', Jeremiah gave English the word 'jeremiad', meaning a long, bitter complaint about the state of society.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Lamentations: These five poems mourn the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC. Several are acrostics, each verse starting with the next Hebrew letter.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Ezekiel: A priest exiled to Babylon, Ezekiel reported strange visions, including a wheel within a wheel and a valley of dry bones that came to life.
Middle books of the Old Testament, in or.Hosea: God tells Hosea to marry an unfaithful wife, Gomer, so that his own painful marriage becomes a living picture of Israel's disloyalty.

Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.А: This letter's name, az, and that of Б, buki, gave the Russian word 'azbuka', meaning alphabet.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.В: It looks like Latin B but sounds like V, and it starts the name of the Russian port Vladivostok.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.Е: It usually sounds like 'ye', and Russian writers often skip the two dots over its cousin Ё.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.К: Looks and sounds like Latin K, as in Кремль, the Kremlin, the fortified heart of Moscow.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.М: It looks like a Latin M and sounds like one, and 'мир' means both 'peace' and 'world'.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.Н: It looks like an H but sounds like N, so Нет, the word for 'no', starts with a letter that looks like an H.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.О: The most common letter in Russian, it looks and sounds like Latin O.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.Р: It looks like a P but sounds like R, so Россия, the Russian name for Russia, starts with it.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.С: It looks like a C but sounds like S, and the Soviet abbreviation СССР uses it three times.
Cyrillic letters that look Latin, in Rus.Х: It looks like Latin X but sounds like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch', as in Хорошо, meaning 'good'.

Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Louvre Pyramid: Designed by I. M. Pei, its glass and metal frame has around 670 panes and was widely mocked before it became beloved.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.El Castillo, Chichén Itzá: The Maya built it so that on the equinoxes a shadow of a snake appears to slither down its staircase.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Pyramid of Cestius, Rome: Built around 12 BC for a Roman magistrate, it was apparently finished in 330 days and later absorbed into the city wall.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Pyramid of Djoser: Designed by Imhotep, it is the earliest large stone building in the world, with stepped layers instead of smooth sides.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Memphis Pyramid arena: This Tennessee arena on the Mississippi River is now a giant store with a hotel and a swamp inside.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Luxor hotel, Las Vegas: A powerful beam of light from its tip is among the strongest in the world.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Pyramid of Khafre (original): It looks taller than the Great Pyramid because it sits on higher ground, and it still has its original casing at the top.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Great Pyramid (original): It was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for nearly 4,000 years, until a medieval cathedral overtook it.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Transamerica Pyramid: This tapering San Francisco skyscraper, finished in 1972, was the city's tallest building until 2018.
Heights of pyramids, ancient and modern.Ryugyong Hotel, Pyongyang: Construction began in 1987, stalled for years and finished only in the 2010s, so it is a hotel that has never fully opened.

Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Couplet: Two rhyming lines; Shakespeare often closed his sonnets with a couplet.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Haiku: Traditional haiku count sounds, 5-7-5, rather than syllables, and Japanese poets traditionally include a seasonal word.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Quatrain: The most common stanza in English poetry, it forms the base of many ballads and hymns.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Limerick: It is named for a city in Ireland, and Edward Lear made it a popular form of nonsense verse.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Sestet: It is the closing six lines of an Italian sonnet, following the eight-line octave.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Ottava rima stanza: Byron used it for his comic epic Don Juan; its rhyme scheme is ABABABCC.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Sonnet: The name comes from the Italian for little song, and Petrarch and Shakespeare made it famous.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Villanelle: Dylan Thomas's 'Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night' is the most famous example, with two repeating refrains.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Ballade: A French form of three eight-line stanzas and a four-line envoi; Francois Villon was its great master.
Poetic forms and stanzas, by number of l.Sestina: Six words rotate as line endings across six stanzas, then a three-line envoi; troubadour Arnaut Daniel invented it.

Volcanoes by height above sea level.Vesuvius: Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 79, and it's still active, overlooking millions in Naples.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Mount St. Helens: Its 1980 eruption blasted away about 400 m from the summit and killed 57 people.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Mount Etna: Europe's tallest active volcano changes height after eruptions, hence the c. in front of its number.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Mount Fuji: Japan's sacred peak last erupted in 1707, and is climbed by hundreds of thousands of people each summer.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Mauna Kea: Measured from the seabed, it is over 10,000 m tall, taller than Everest.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Mount Rainier: Seattle lies in its shadow, and the mountain bears more glacier ice than any other peak in the lower 48 states.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Popocatépetl: Its Nahuatl name means the smoking mountain, and it frequently puffs ash near Mexico City.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Kilimanjaro: Africa's highest peak is a dormant volcano, whose snowcaps have been shrinking for decades.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Chimborazo: Because of Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the farthest point from the Earth's center, farther than Everest.
Volcanoes by height above sea level.Ojos del Salado: Rising on the Chile-Argentina border, it is the world's highest active volcano.

Count them!.Humps on a Bactrian camel: Bactrian camels have two humps and dromedaries one, and the humps store fat, not water.
Count them!.Body sections of an insect: Head, thorax and abdomen define an insect, so two-section spiders are not insects.
Count them!.Wings on a dragonfly: Dragonflies move each of their four wings independently, letting them hover and even fly backward.
Count them!.Arms on a starfish: Many can regrow lost arms, and some species regenerate a whole body from a single arm.
Count them!.Legs on an ant: All insects have six legs, and ants walk with a tripod gait, moving three at a time.
Count them!.Eyes on most spiders: Most spiders have eight eyes but see poorly, while jumping spiders have excellent vision.
Count them!.Arms and tentacles on a squid: Squid have eight arms plus two longer feeding tentacles, making ten appendages.
Count them!.Ribs in a human: Humans have 12 pairs of ribs, though some people have an extra one growing from the neck.
Count them!.Teeth in a cat: Adult cats have 30 teeth, including sharp carnassials designed for shearing meat.
Count them!.Teeth in a pig: Adult pigs have 44 teeth, reflecting an omnivorous diet like ours.

Safety inventions, in order.Lightning rod: Benjamin Franklin proposed it in the 1750s, after studying electricity, and it protects buildings by guiding strikes safely to the ground.
Safety inventions, in order.Davy safety lamp: Sir Humphry Davy's wire mesh around the flame stopped lamps from igniting the methane that caused deadly coal mine explosions.
Safety inventions, in order.Portable fire extinguisher: British army officer George Manby made it from a copper vessel filled with a potash solution, driven out by compressed air.
Safety inventions, in order.Safety match: The safe version put phosphorus on the box's striking strip rather than the match head, so matches could no longer ignite by accident.
Safety inventions, in order.Otis safety elevator: Elisha Otis proved it at a New York fair by cutting the lift's rope himself, then announcing, All safe, gentlemen.
Safety inventions, in order.Gas mask: They were developed after chlorine gas attacks in World War I, and early versions used cloth soaked in chemicals.
Safety inventions, in order.Hard hat: The Bullard company's version was made for shipyard workers, and they became famous during building of the Hoover Dam.
Safety inventions, in order.Crash test dummy: Sierra Sam, built by Samuel Alderson, was made to test ejection seats for the US Air Force before cars.
Safety inventions, in order.Three-point seatbelt: Volvo's Nils Bohlin invented it, and Volvo gave the patent away free to all carmakers because it saved lives.
Safety inventions, in order.Home smoke detector: Duane Pearsall and Stanley Peterson made the first affordable, battery-powered version, and it spread rapidly in the 1970s.

Calories in one tablespoon.Water: A US tablespoon is about 15 milliliters, though Australian tablespoons are a larger 20, so recipes can quietly differ across countries.
Calories in one tablespoon.Yellow mustard: Yellow mustard gets its color from turmeric, and its light taste comes from ground mustard seed mixed with vinegar.
Calories in one tablespoon.Soy sauce: Brewed from fermented soybeans and wheat, it packs close to 900 mg of sodium per tablespoon, a huge share of a daily limit.
Calories in one tablespoon.Ketchup: It descends from a fermented fish sauce, from the Hokkien ke-tsiap, and tomato only joined the recipe in the 1800s.
Calories in one tablespoon.Hummus: The word hummus is simply Arabic for chickpeas, and the dip's full name means chickpeas with tahini.
Calories in one tablespoon.Granulated sugar: Table sugar has about four calories per gram, so it is quite a bit less calorie dense than the oil or butter in this list.
Calories in one tablespoon.Honey: Bees visit about two million flowers to make a pound of honey, so each tablespoon represents a vast amount of foraging.
Calories in one tablespoon.Peanut butter: Peanut butter is not made of nuts, because peanuts are legumes that grow underground, like beans.
Calories in one tablespoon.Butter: A tablespoon is one eighth of a standard US stick of butter, which is why recipes use that handy marking on the wrapper.
Calories in one tablespoon.Olive oil: It is pure fat at nine calories per gram, so no common tablespoon beats it, even though it is one of the healthier fats.

When these board and card games hit stor.Monopoly (Parker Brothers): Parker Brothers bought Charles Darrow's version, but it grew from Elizabeth Magie's Landlord's Game, designed to show how land monopolies harm tenants.
When these board and card games hit stor.Scrabble: Architect Alfred Butts devised it as 'Criss-Crosses' after counting letter frequencies in newspapers, which is how the tile values were set.
When these board and card games hit stor.Risk: French filmmaker Albert Lamorisse invented it as 'La Conquête du Monde'; he also directed the short film The Red Balloon.
When these board and card games hit stor.Twister: It surged after Johnny Carson played it on television with Eva Gabor in 1966, when a mat of players tangling up made great viewing.
When these board and card games hit stor.Uno: A barber from Ohio, Merle Robbins, invented it and first sold copies himself, before the rights were bought by what became Mattel.
When these board and card games hit stor.Trivial Pursuit: Two Canadian journalists dreamed it up in 1979 over a Scrabble game missing pieces; it has since sold over 100 million copies.
When these board and card games hit stor.Pictionary: Inventor Rob Angel was a Seattle waiter; the name blends 'picture' and 'dictionary', and players sketch clues against a timer.
When these board and card games hit stor.Catan: Released in Germany as Die Siedler von Catan, it sold tens of millions of copies and helped start the modern board game boom.
When these board and card games hit stor.Pandemic: Matt Leacock's design has players cooperate against spreading diseases rather than each other, helping popularise co-operative board games.
When these board and card games hit stor.Cards Against Humanity: Launched via a crowdfunding campaign by a group of friends, it is free to print, and its Black Friday stunts included selling nothing at all.

Children's authors, by birth year.Hans Christian Andersen: Andersen wrote The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling, and a famous statue of his mermaid sits in Copenhagen.
Children's authors, by birth year.Lewis Carroll: His real name was Charles Dodgson, and he lectured in mathematics at Oxford.
Children's authors, by birth year.L. Frank Baum: He wrote fourteen Oz novels, beyond the famous first one.
Children's authors, by birth year.Beatrix Potter: Her book royalties helped her buy Lake District farmland, which she left to the National Trust.
Children's authors, by birth year.A.A. Milne: Winnie-the-Pooh was named after a real bear at London Zoo called Winnipeg.
Children's authors, by birth year.Dr. Seuss: Born Theodor Geisel, he wrote Green Eggs and Ham using only 50 different words, after a bet.
Children's authors, by birth year.Astrid Lindgren: She invented Pippi Longstocking to entertain her daughter, who was ill in bed.
Children's authors, by birth year.Roald Dahl: Before writing, he was a Royal Air Force fighter pilot in World War II.
Children's authors, by birth year.Maurice Sendak: His 1963 classic was originally to be about wild horses, until he realized he could not draw them.
Children's authors, by birth year.Judy Blume: Her books often dealt frankly with growing up and were frequently banned in schools.

Asian animals by weight.Philippine tarsier: Each eye is about as big as its whole brain, and it can swivel its head nearly 180 degrees to spot insects while hunting at night.
Asian animals by weight.Slow loris: It is one of the few venomous mammals: it licks a gland on its elbow, mixes the secretion with saliva, and delivers a toxic bite.
Asian animals by weight.Red panda: Despite the name and the false thumb it uses to grip bamboo, it is not closely related to giant pandas; it sits in a family of its own.
Asian animals by weight.Proboscis monkey (male): Males carry a huge drooping nose that likely amplifies their honking calls and attracts mates. The species lives only on Borneo, near rivers and mangroves.
Asian animals by weight.Snow leopard: It cannot roar, but its thick, long tail helps it balance on cliffs, and it can leap about 15 meters across a gap.
Asian animals by weight.Giant panda: Pandas have a meat-eater's gut yet eat bamboo up to 14 hours a day, and a newborn weighs only about 100 grams, a thousandth of its mother's weight.
Asian animals by weight.Bengal tiger: The stripes aren't only in the fur: each tiger's pattern is unique, and the skin beneath the stripes is striped too.
Asian animals by weight.Gaur: The largest wild cattle on Earth, with a muscular shoulder ridge and pale lower legs, it lives in South and Southeast Asian forests; adults fear little besides tigers.
Asian animals by weight.Indian rhino: Its folded, armor-like skin looks riveted, and it has just one horn. Kaziranga National Park in Assam shelters about two thirds of the world's population.
Asian animals by weight.Asian elephant: Smaller-eared than African elephants, it has a twin-domed head and a single fingerlike tip on its trunk. People have worked alongside it for thousands of years.

Hit mobile games by release.Snake (Nokia): Nokia preloaded it on the 6110 in 1997, and it became one of the most played games ever, reaching hundreds of millions of phones.
Hit mobile games by release.Angry Birds: Rovio reportedly made around 50 games before this one hit; the Finnish studio's bird-slinging puzzle became one of the first big smartphone sensations.
Hit mobile games by release.Fruit Ninja: Australian studio Halfbrick built it around swiping, a gesture that suited touchscreens perfectly, and it has been downloaded over a billion times.
Hit mobile games by release.Temple Run: Imangi Studios, a husband-and-wife team in North Carolina, made it, and it popularized the endless-runner genre on phones.
Hit mobile games by release.Candy Crush Saga: King's match-three hit began on Facebook in 2012, and Activision Blizzard bought King for about $5.9 billion in 2016.
Hit mobile games by release.Flappy Bird: Solo developer Dong Nguyen pulled it from app stores in 2014 at the height of its fame, saying its popularity had spoiled his simple life.
Hit mobile games by release.Monument Valley: Developed by ustwo games, this puzzler of impossible architecture draws on M.C. Escher's drawings and won an Apple Design Award.
Hit mobile games by release.Pokemon Go: Niantic built it on the map data of its earlier game Ingress, and it passed 500 million downloads in about two months.
Hit mobile games by release.Among Us: Innersloth released it in 2018, but it exploded in 2020 during lockdowns, when streamers made its bluffing and betrayal a worldwide craze.
Hit mobile games by release.Genshin Impact: miHoYo's open-world game launched on mobile, PC and PlayStation at once, and reportedly earned over a billion dollars within its first year.

Public health milestones.Semmelweis orders handwashing: The Hungarian doctor found that washing hands with chlorinated lime slashed deaths from childbed fever, but colleagues largely rejected him.
Public health milestones.John Snow's cholera map: He mapped cholera deaths around London's Broad Street pump and had its handle removed, a founding moment for epidemiology.
Public health milestones.Red Cross founded: Henri Dunant founded it after witnessing the Battle of Solferino, and won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
Public health milestones.First city water fluoridation: Grand Rapids, Michigan, added fluoride to its water, after studies showed lower tooth decay where it occurred naturally.
Public health milestones.World Health Organization: It became a United Nations agency and later led the campaign that wiped out smallpox.
Public health milestones.Surgeon General on smoking: The report linking smoking to lung cancer helped cut US adult smoking from over 40 percent to roughly 12 percent.
Public health milestones.First seatbelt law (Victoria): Victoria in Australia was the first place in the world to make wearing seat belts compulsory, and road deaths fell.
Public health milestones.USDA Food Pyramid: Grains formed its wide base at six to eleven servings a day, a design later critics said overweighted carbohydrates.
Public health milestones.Ireland bans smoking at work: Ireland was the first country to ban smoking in all workplaces, pubs included, a model many nations then copied.
Public health milestones.MyPlate replaces the pyramid: It swapped the pyramid for a plate divided into fruits, vegetables, grains and protein, with a dairy circle beside it.

Finding your way: navigation milestones.Ptolemy's Geography: Ptolemy catalogued thousands of places by latitude and longitude, shaping mapmaking for over a thousand years.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Compass used at sea: Early compasses were magnetized needles floating in water, and Chinese records of that era describe sailors using them at sea.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Mercator's map: His projection keeps compass bearings as straight lines, ideal for sailors, but inflates areas near the poles.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Eddystone lighthouse: Henry Winstanley built it on a wave-battered rock off Plymouth, and died inside it when a great storm destroyed it in 1703.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Hadley's octant: John Hadley's reflecting instrument let navigators measure the Sun's height at sea, and the sextant descended from it.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Harrison's H4 chronometer: John Harrison's watch lost only seconds on a transatlantic voyage, solving the longitude problem.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Ordnance Survey founded: Britain's national mapping agency began by surveying the south coast against a feared French invasion; hence the word 'ordnance'.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Greenwich prime meridian: The 1884 conference in Washington chose Greenwich as the zero of longitude, with France abstaining.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Gyrocompass: It finds true north using a spinning wheel and Earth's rotation, unaffected by magnetism, which suits steel ships.
Finding your way: navigation milestones.Radar: Robert Watson-Watt demonstrated radio detection of aircraft, and Britain's radar chain helped win the Battle of Britain.

Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Loosehead prop: Sits on the left of the scrum, where his job is to hold up huge weight and drive forward with the hooker beside him.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Hooker: He hooks the ball back with his foot in the scrum, and usually throws the ball in at lineouts to his jumpers.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Tighthead prop: The name comes from his head being jammed 'tight' against the opposing loosehead prop, so he takes the heaviest scrum pressure.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Blindside flanker: Positioned on the shorter side of the scrum, nearest the touchline, so this flanker defends the narrow channel.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Openside flanker: Often a specialist at winning the ball at the breakdown by stealing it off the ground, a skill nicknamed 'jackalling'.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Scrum-half: The link between forwards and backs who feeds the ball into the scrum and passes from rucks, so he is in the game constantly.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Fly-half: The playmaker who directs the attack, and often does the goalkicking, which is why this number is so prized.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Inside centre: In New Zealand this position is called second five-eighth, one of rugby's many regional names for the same job.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Outside centre: Brian O'Driscoll made this shirt famous for Ireland and the Lions, playing at the very end of the backline.
Rugby union shirt numbers by position.Fullback: The last line of defence, who also catches high kicks and launches counterattacks from deep behind the rest.

American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Y2K: The society also picked 'jazz' as the word of the century in the same vote, which makes this pick feel even odder.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Chad: It came from the 'hanging chads' of the Florida ballot recount that settled the US presidential election.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Metrosexual: Coined in 1994 by writer Mark Simpson, it was popularised in the early 2000s for urban men who cared about grooming.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Plutoed: It means to demote someone or something, after Pluto lost its status as a planet.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Tweet: It rose with the social network; the word was voted Word of the Year and became an everyday verb.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.App: Short for 'application', it exploded with the smartphone, and the vote reflected how apps took over daily life.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Hashtag: The pound sign took on a new life as a way to tag posts on social media, and the word jumped into everyday speech.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Dumpster fire: It describes a chaotic mess, and won the 2016 vote at the end of a very turbulent election year.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Covid: A shortened form of coronavirus disease, it became the word of 2020 as the pandemic shaped everything.
American Dialect Society Words of the Ye.Enshittification: Cory Doctorow coined it for how online platforms get worse over time, as they squeeze users and business.

Streaming services by launch.iTunes Store: Apple's store launched with 200,000 songs and sold 1 million of them in its first week, helping to persuade a doubtful music industry about digital sales.
Streaming services by launch.Vimeo: Vimeo launched in 2004, a year before YouTube, and it began as a place for filmmakers to share artistic work. Its name is a play on 'video' and 'me'.
Streaming services by launch.Pandora: This internet radio service grew out of the Music Genome Project, where musicians tagged songs by qualities to recommend similar tracks.
Streaming services by launch.Netflix streaming: The service began by mailing DVDs; its first streaming offering, a small library, helped it pivot into one of the biggest media companies.
Streaming services by launch.Hulu: Its name is a blend of hula and Hulu, a Mandarin word meaning 'precious gourd', and it began as a joint venture of major U.S. networks.
Streaming services by launch.Twitch: It started as Justin.tv, one person's broadcast of his life, and later it pivoted to game streaming before Amazon bought it for nearly a billion dollars.
Streaming services by launch.Tidal: Jay-Z and other artists relaunched it as a service that focused on high-fidelity sound and that put artists' ownership front and centre.
Streaming services by launch.Apple Music: It was built from Beats Music after Apple bought the headphone company for about 3 billion dollars, its largest acquisition at the time.
Streaming services by launch.Disney+: It signed up more than 10 million people on its first day, and it reached tens of millions within months by using Marvel, Pixar and Star Wars.
Streaming services by launch.HBO Max: Its name was later shortened when it rebranded, and it launched during the early pandemic with Warner Bros films and HBO shows.

Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Wells Fargo: Henry Wells and William Fargo started it during the California Gold Rush to carry gold and mail, and the stagecoach is still its logo.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Pony Express: This legendary mail route used fast riders and relays, and it ran for only about 18 months before the telegraph made it obsolete.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.UPS: It began as a messenger service in Seattle, and its brown trucks come from the founder's belief that the colour looks professional and hides dirt.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Greyhound: The bus company's running-dog logo helps it stand out, and it started as a service carrying miners between two Minnesota towns.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.DHL: Its founders came from Hawaii's mail routes, and its letters stand for the three founders' surnames: Dalsey, Hillblom and Lynn.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.FedEx: John Enders' team isolated the measles virus in 1954, and the vaccine that followed cut cases dramatically, though the disease still returns where vaccination lapses.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Grubhub: The online platform started in Chicago as a way to order food from local restaurants for delivery.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Postmates: A bicycle courier company founded in San Francisco was purchased by Uber for about 2.7 billion dollars.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.Lyft: The ride-hailing company began as Zimride and it is known for its pink moustache logo, which was dropped in 2015.
Delivery and transport companies, by fou.DoorDash: Started by Stanford students as a Palo Alto delivery site, it grew into the biggest food-delivery app in the U.S.

Quirky special days through the year.Burns Night: Scots mark Robert Burns's birthday with haggis, whisky and his poem Address to a Haggis, read aloud as the dish arrives.
Quirky special days through the year.Groundhog Day: In Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, a groundhog named Phil has been consulted since 1887 for whether winter will last.
Quirky special days through the year.Pi Day: Physicist Larry Shaw started it in 1988 at San Francisco's Exploratorium, and it falls on Einstein's birthday.
Quirky special days through the year.The Ides of March: Julius Caesar was assassinated on this date in 44 BC, and in the Roman calendar Ides simply meant mid-month.
Quirky special days through the year.Star Wars Day: The pun May the Fourth be with you was first used in a 1979 London newspaper ad congratulating Margaret Thatcher.
Quirky special days through the year.Towel Day: Fans began wearing towels two weeks after Douglas Adams died in 2001, in honour of the Hitchhiker's Guide.
Quirky special days through the year.Bloomsday: James Joyce set his novel Ulysses on this day in 1904, and fans in Dublin retrace its route in costume.
Quirky special days through the year.Talk Like a Pirate Day: Two friends in Oregon invented it in 1995, and it spread worldwide after a humour columnist, Dave Barry, wrote about it.
Quirky special days through the year.World Kindness Day: It has been observed since 1998 and was launched by a movement of groups promoting kindness around the world.
Quirky special days through the year.Boxing Day: It has nothing to do with the sport and probably comes from the tradition of giving Christmas boxes to servants and tradespeople.

Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Earth's surface: Earth's surface is the base of the atmosphere, held in place by gravity, with half its mass lying below about 5.5 km.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Troposphere: The troposphere holds about three-quarters of the air by mass and nearly all weather, and it gets colder with height.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Tropopause: The tropopause marks the top of the weather layer, jets cruise near it, and it is higher at the equator than at the poles.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Stratosphere: The ozone layer sits in the stratosphere and absorbs ultraviolet light, which warms the air as you go higher.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Stratopause: At the top of the stratosphere, the air is at its warmest, around the freezing point, before temperatures start falling again.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Mesosphere: Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere, making shooting stars; it is also very cold, down to about -90 °C.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Mesopause: The mesopause is the coldest place in Earth's atmosphere, around -90 °C, where glowing noctilucent clouds can form.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Thermosphere: Auroras glow in the thermosphere, and the International Space Station orbits there; its thin air is extremely hot yet would feel cold.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Thermopause: The thermopause, also called the exobase, is where the air becomes so thin that particles rarely collide.
Layers of the sky, from the ground up.Exosphere: The exosphere fades into space, with mostly hydrogen and helium so sparse that atoms can escape Earth's gravity.

When these places abolished slavery.Chile: Chile was one of the first Latin American countries to abolish slavery, soon after winning independence.
When these places abolished slavery.Mexico: President Vicente Guerrero, who was of African descent, decreed abolition in Mexico in 1829.
When these places abolished slavery.British Empire: The Slavery Abolition Act compensated slave owners, not the enslaved; the British debt for this was only paid off in 2015.
When these places abolished slavery.France: France abolished it in 1794 and Napoleon restored it in 1802, then it ended for good in 1848.
When these places abolished slavery.Netherlands: Slavery ended in Dutch colonies in 1863, but in Suriname those freed had to work another ten years under state supervision.
When these places abolished slavery.United States: The Thirteenth Amendment ended slavery in December 1865, but allowed forced labor as punishment for crime.
When these places abolished slavery.Puerto Rico: Abolition in Puerto Rico, under Spanish rule, compensated slaveholders, and freed people had to work for three more years.
When these places abolished slavery.Cuba: Cuba, still Spanish, was among the last in the Americas, ending slavery in 1886 after a phase-out.
When these places abolished slavery.Brazil: Brazil's Golden Law, signed by Princess Isabel, made it the last country in the Americas to end slavery, freeing roughly 700,000 people.
When these places abolished slavery.Mauritania: Mauritania was the last country to formally abolish slavery, in 1981, and made it a crime in 2007, but it persists.

Big number names (US short scale), by si.billion: British usage once defined 'billion' as a million million; the American short-scale meaning is now standard in English.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.trillion: A trillion seconds is about 31,700 years, a good way to feel how big it really is.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.quadrillion: Estimates put the world's ants at around 20 quadrillion.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.quintillion: An exabyte is a quintillion bytes, a unit now used for global internet traffic.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.sextillion: Estimates of the stars in the observable universe run from sextillions to septillions.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.septillion: The SI prefix 'yotta' stands for this size.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.octillion: The SI prefix 'ronna' for 10^27 was added in 2022, with 'quetta' for 10^30.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.decillion: The name jumps from nonillion at 10^30, so skipping a step puts this one at 10^33.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.googol: Mathematician Edward Kasner's nine-year-old nephew coined it around 1920, and it inspired the name Google.
Big number names (US short scale), by si.centillion: A one followed by 303 zeros, yet it is vanishingly tiny next to a googolplex.

When these novelty toys hit shelves.Whoopee cushion: A rubber bladder that imitates a rude noise when sat on, it has been a prank staple for nearly a century.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Slinky: Engineer Richard James dropped a tension spring and watched it 'walk', and the toy sold out at a Philadelphia store in 1945.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Silly Putty: It grew from a failed attempt to make synthetic rubber in WWII and can lift newsprint images.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Sea-Monkeys: These are actually brine shrimp, which hatch from dried eggs in water; the ads promised 'instant life'.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Lava lamp: Edward Craven Walker invented it in Britain, inspired by an egg timer he saw in a pub.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Pet Rock: Gary Dahl sold ordinary rocks in a box as 'pets' and became a millionaire within months.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Chia Pet: The terracotta figures sprout chia seeds as 'fur', and the ch-ch-ch-chia jingle became famous.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Tamagotchi: This Japanese virtual pet needed feeding and cleaning; the name blends 'tamago', egg, with 'watch'.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Furby: It sold tens of millions within a few years, and its toys 'learned' English as they were played with.
When these novelty toys hit shelves.Big Mouth Billy Bass: The motion-triggered fish sang 'Take Me to the River' and 'Don't Worry, Be Happy'.

When these inventions first appeared.Farming: Began in the Fertile Crescent of the Middle East, when people started growing wild wheat and barley.
When these inventions first appeared.The wheel: The earliest wheels were potters' wheels in Mesopotamia, with cart wheels following soon after.
When these inventions first appeared.The alphabet: The first alphabet emerged in Egypt's Sinai region, and Phoenician letters later led to Greek and Latin ones.
When these inventions first appeared.Coins: Made of a gold-silver alloy called electrum, they were first minted in Lydia, in modern Turkey.
When these inventions first appeared.Antikythera mechanism: A hand-cranked Greek device recovered from a shipwreck in 1901 that predicted eclipses, often called the first analog computer.
When these inventions first appeared.Paper, per Cai Lun: Cai Lun was a Han court official who improved paper-making, using bark, rags and fishing nets.
When these inventions first appeared.Gunpowder: Chinese alchemists seeking an elixir of life discovered it by accident.
When these inventions first appeared.Movable type: Bi Sheng carved individual ceramic characters in Song China, centuries before Gutenberg.
When these inventions first appeared.Eyeglasses: Spectacles first appeared in Italy, and made reading and fine work possible for many older people.
When these inventions first appeared.Gutenberg's printing press: His Mainz workshop printed the Gutenberg Bible, of which about 180 copies were made.

Word count of these famous texts.Gettysburg Address: Lincoln spoke for about two minutes after the main speaker had talked for two hours, and the other speaker praised his brevity.
Word count of these famous texts.Declaration of Independence: Thomas Jefferson drafted it in about two weeks, and Congress cut his passage condemning the slave trade.
Word count of these famous texts.US Constitution (original): Seven articles, readable in about half an hour; it is among the shortest written national constitutions still in use.
Word count of these famous texts.The Old Man and the Sea: Hemingway's slim novella won the 1953 Pulitzer and helped earn him the 1954 Nobel Prize.
Word count of these famous texts.The Great Gatsby: It sold poorly in Fitzgerald's lifetime and only became a staple of classrooms after his death.
Word count of these famous texts.Harry Potter book 1: After about a dozen rejections, Bloomsbury took it on, reportedly after the chairman's eight-year-old daughter loved the first chapter.
Word count of these famous texts.The Hobbit: Tolkien began it as a bedtime story for his children; its success led to The Lord of the Rings.
Word count of these famous texts.Moby-Dick: Melville's whale epic flopped in his lifetime, and has entire chapters on whale anatomy.
Word count of these famous texts.War and Peace (English): Tolstoy's epic follows five aristocratic families through Napoleon's invasion, and translations vary, so counts differ.
Word count of these famous texts.King James Bible: About 47 scholars produced it in 1611, and it gave English idioms like 'the powers that be'.

When these energy and sports drinks laun.Lucozade: Created in Newcastle as Glucozade for sick patients, it was later rebranded to sell to athletes.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Lipovitan D: This Japanese vitamin tonic drink is sold in a small brown bottle, and it is one of the world's early energy drinks.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Krating Daeng: The Thai drink, whose name means "red gaur", was the model for Red Bull, and it was popular with truck drivers and workers.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Jolt Cola: Its slogan promised "all the sugar and twice the caffeine", and it was a hit with students in the 1980s.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Red Bull: An Austrian businessman tasted a Thai energy drink on a trip, adapted it, and then built a brand around extreme sports.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Rockstar: Founded by the son of a radio talk host, the brand grew by sponsoring music festivals and extreme sports, aiming at young drinkers.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Monster Energy: The brand's claw logo has been on cans since 2002, and its maker Hansen's later sold a share to Coca-Cola.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.5-hour Energy: The small two-ounce bottles were designed so it could be sold at checkout counters, and it was created by Manoj Bhargava.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Bang: Launched in Florida, the brand was pushed hard on social media and sold in neon cans, and its maker later faced a long legal fight with Monster.
When these energy and sports drinks laun.Prime: A viral hit in 2022 created by two YouTubers, so scarce at first that bottles were resold online.

Finnish month names, in calendar order.tammikuu: Tammi means oak but also the 'heart' of a tree; tammikuu is the heart of winter, when the sun is barely up in northern Finland.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.helmikuu: Helmi means pearl, and helmikuu may refer to frozen droplets on branches, like pearls of ice, shimmering in winter.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.huhtikuu: Huhta refers to land cleared by slash-and-burn farming, an old method that shaped Finnish agriculture in the spring.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.toukokuu: Touko is an old word for sowing, so this month is when Finnish farmers traditionally planted their fields.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.kesäkuu: Kesä means summer, and this month brings Juhannus, midsummer, when Finns celebrate with bonfires under nearly endless daylight.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.heinäkuu: Heinä means hay, so this is literally 'hay month', when grass was cut and dried for livestock to eat through winter.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.elokuu: Elo means grain or harvest, and this is the month when fields turn golden and crops are brought in.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.syyskuu: Syys means autumn, and syyskuu brings ruska, the spectacular fall foliage season, in Finnish Lapland.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.marraskuu: Marras comes from an old word for death, so marraskuu is 'death month', when nature seems to die in the dark of November.
Finnish month names, in calendar order.joulukuu: Joulu comes from the Old Norse word for Yule, so joulukuu is Christmas month, and it ends the year with long nights.

Fill in the number: everyday idioms.Back to square ___: Its origin is debated, with board games and 1930s radio football commentary, which used numbered squares, as rival theories.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.___ in the bush (bird in hand): The proverb is centuries old, and a version of it appears in English as early as the 15th century.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.___ sheets to the wind: A 'sheet' here is a rope controlling a sail, and loose ones make a ship stagger like a drunk.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.Down on all ___: Cats and dogs walk on their toes, not the whole foot, unlike humans.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.Take ___ (have a break): Dave Brubeck's jazz hit 'Take Five' is written in 5/4 time and became the first jazz single to sell a million copies.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.At ___ and sevens: Chaucer used a phrase like it, which comes from an old dice game, so it means disorder.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.In ___ heaven: Many religions describe seven heavens, with the seventh the highest, the place of ultimate bliss.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.Behind the ___ ball: In one form of pool, the black eight ball must be potted last, and pocketing it too soon loses the game.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.On cloud ___: It is often traced to an old weather-bureau cloud classification that ranked the highest clouds ninth.
Fill in the number: everyday idioms.Hang ___ (surfing): The surfer's trick puts all ten toes over the front edge of the board.

Typical weight of these fish we eat.Whitebait: Not a species but the tiny young of herring or sprat, eaten whole, which is why these fish are served with heads and all.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Anchovy: Salty and intense, anchovies hide in Caesar dressing and Worcestershire sauce, adding savory depth without a fishy taste.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Sardine: Named for Sardinia, where they were once abundant; these small oily fish school in the billions and feed many larger predators.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Mackerel: Mackerel must keep swimming to breathe water over its gills, and its oily flesh is rich in omega-3 fats.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Rainbow trout: Steelhead are the same species that head to sea and return to freshwater to spawn, growing far larger than lake-bound trout.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Atlantic salmon: Atlantic salmon find their birth river by smell, and almost all of those sold today come from fish farms, not the wild.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Atlantic cod: Newfoundland's cod fishery collapsed in 1992 after centuries of abundance, and a moratorium on fishing was declared.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Pacific halibut: Halibut start life with an eye on each side, then one eye migrates as the fish settles, ending with both on one side.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Swordfish: Swordfish can warm their eyes and brain with a special heater organ, which helps them hunt in the cold deep.
Typical weight of these fish we eat.Bluefin tuna: A single bluefin sold for about $3.1 million at Tokyo's Toyosu market in 2019, the highest price ever paid for a fish.

Clothing chains, by founding year.Abercrombie & Fitch: Founded as an outfitter for fishermen and explorers. Theodore Roosevelt and Ernest Hemingway were among its customers.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Topshop: Started as a youth fashion section inside a Sheffield department store. The brand collapsed in 2020 and was later revived online.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Gap: Donald and Doris Fisher opened it in San Francisco to sell Levi's jeans, after he could not find a pair that fit.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Zara: Amancio Ortega's first store opened in A Coruña, Spain. Its fast-fashion model can take a design from sketch to shops in weeks.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Banana Republic: Started as a safari-themed travel clothing shop by Mel and Patricia Ziegler. Gap bought it in 1983.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Uniqlo: The name is short for 'Unique Clothing Warehouse'. The brand began in Hiroshima, Japan.
Clothing chains, by founding year.American Apparel: Founded by Dov Charney and known for 'Made in Downtown LA' basics. It filed for bankruptcy in 2015.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Old Navy: Gap launched it as a cheaper sister brand, aiming at family shoppers.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Shein: Started in Nanjing, China, it ships worldwide and adds thousands of new styles to its site daily.
Clothing chains, by founding year.Everlane: Founded in San Francisco, it built its image on 'radical transparency', revealing what its factories charge.

Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Morphine: Friedrich Sertürner isolated it from opium, the first active ingredient extracted from a plant; named for Morpheus, god of dreams.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Quinine: Extracted from cinchona bark, it treated malaria for centuries and still gives tonic water its bitter taste.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Aspirin: Chemist Felix Hoffmann at Bayer made a gentler form of a compound from willow bark; 'Aspirin' was Bayer's brand name.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Insulin: In 1922 a 14-year-old Leonard Thompson, dying of diabetes, became the first patient; the Toronto team won a Nobel Prize.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Penicillin: Alexander Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria on a neglected dish; Florey and Chain later turned it into a drug.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Streptomycin: Found in soil bacteria by Selman Waksman's lab, it was the first effective antibiotic against tuberculosis; he coined 'antibiotic'.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.The contraceptive pill: Enovid, approved in the US in 1960, was the first oral contraceptive and reshaped family planning.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Valium: Roche's diazepam became the best-selling drug in the world in the 1970s; the Rolling Stones' 'Mother's Little Helper' is about such pills.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Prozac: Eli Lilly's fluoxetine, approved in 1987, was the first widely used SSRI antidepressant.
Medicines, by when they were found or fi.Viagra: Pfizer first tested it as a heart drug, but side effects seen in trial volunteers pointed it toward its famous use.

Video game movies by release.Super Mario Bros. (Hoskins): Bob Hoskins and John Leguizamo starred in this flop, and Hoskins later called it the worst thing he ever did.
Video game movies by release.Mortal Kombat (original): Its techno theme, 'Techno Syndrome', became a club hit and is now among the best-known video game film tunes.
Video game movies by release.Lara Croft: Tomb Raider: Angelina Jolie did many of her own stunts, and some scenes were shot at Cambodia's Ta Prohm temple, wrapped in tree roots.
Video game movies by release.Resident Evil: Milla Jovovich's film spawned a franchise of six films, a rare video game adaptation that kept going.
Video game movies by release.Prince of Persia: Disney's adventure was based on the game 'The Sands of Time', created by Jordan Mechner of the original Prince of Persia.
Video game movies by release.Warcraft: Director Duncan Jones's film earned most of its money in China, where the games have a huge following.
Video game movies by release.Detective Pikachu: Ryan Reynolds voiced Pikachu, the first live-action Pokémon movie, with a mix of real sets and digital creatures.
Video game movies by release.Sonic the Hedgehog: The studio redesigned Sonic after fans mocked the first trailer, a rare case of a movie changing its look after public backlash.
Video game movies by release.The Super Mario Bros. Movie: It became the highest-grossing video game movie ever, helped by the Mario theme and nostalgic fans of all ages.
Video game movies by release.A Minecraft Movie: Jack Black stars, and the 'chicken jockey' moment from the film became a meme that spread among audiences.

The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ariel misses the concert: Disney's 1989 The Little Mermaid kicked off the Disney Renaissance, a run of hit animated musicals through the 1990s.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ariel rescues Eric at sea: The rescue echoes Hans Christian Andersen's 1837 original, where the mermaid saves a prince from a shipwreck.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Triton wrecks her grotto: King Triton is named for the Greek sea god Triton, the trumpet-blowing son of Poseidon.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ariel's deal with Ursula: In Andersen's original, the sea witch cuts out the mermaid's tongue, and every step on land feels like walking on knives.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ariel gets legs: Ariel's movements were partly modelled on live-action reference of actress Sherri Stoner, a common animation technique.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Eric finds her on the beach: Eric's dog Max is an Old English sheepdog, and his chase after Ariel and her friends is a comic highlight.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.\"Kiss the Girl\" boat ride: Kiss the Girl is a calypso-style number by Alan Menken and Howard Ashman, performed by Sebastian the crab.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ursula poses as Vanessa: Vanessa is voiced by Jodi Benson, who is also Ariel's own speaking and singing voice.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Ariel disrupts the wedding: The shell necklace holding Ariel's voice is the key to breaking the spell, and her sea friends fight to get it.
The Little Mermaid, in story order.Eric rams Ursula with a ship: Ursula's grand finale as a giant was inspired by the drag performer Divine, who also influenced her look.

Islamic history through the ages.The Hijra to Medina: The journey from Mecca to Medina marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
Islamic history through the ages.Umayyad caliphate begins: From Damascus, this dynasty ruled a vast area stretching from Spain to Central Asia.
Islamic history through the ages.Abbasid revolution: The revolution moved the capital east to Iraq, and the dynasty presided over a golden age of science and learning.
Islamic history through the ages.Baghdad founded: Caliph al-Mansur built the Round City, also called the City of Peace, on the Tigris.
Islamic history through the ages.Great Mosque of Córdoba begun: Its forest of red-and-white striped arches is stunning; after the Reconquista, a cathedral was built inside it.
Islamic history through the ages.Cairo founded: The Fatimids founded the city and also al-Azhar, one of the world's oldest universities, still running.
Islamic history through the ages.Saladin retakes Jerusalem: After winning at Hattin, he retook the city, and treated its inhabitants relatively mercifully.
Islamic history through the ages.Mongols sack Baghdad: Hulagu Khan's army destroyed the city; legend says the Tigris ran black with ink from the libraries' books.
Islamic history through the ages.Ottomans take Constantinople: Mehmed II used giant cannons to breach the walls; the city became Istanbul, and the Hagia Sophia a mosque.
Islamic history through the ages.Caliphate abolished: Turkey's new republic under Ataturk ended an institution that had lasted nearly thirteen centuries.

The record for digits of π.William Shanks, 1873: Shanks spent years computing by hand, but only the first 527 digits were correct; the error was found in 1944.
The record for digits of π.ENIAC, 1949: One of the first electronic computers, ENIAC took about 70 hours to calculate this many digits, a huge leap over hand calculation.
The record for digits of π.IBM 7090, 1961: This transistor-based mainframe took under nine hours to reach over a hundred thousand digits, showing how fast computers were advancing.
The record for digits of π.Guilloud and Bouyer, 1973: This French pair reached a million digits using a CDC 7600 supercomputer, a landmark in the number's long history.
The record for digits of π.Chudnovsky brothers, 1989: The two mathematicians built their own supercomputer in a New York apartment, and their formula is still used by record setters today.
The record for digits of π.Yasumasa Kanada, 1999: A Tokyo professor who held the record repeatedly through the 1980s to 2000s, Kanada used supercomputers at the University of Tokyo.
The record for digits of π.Yasumasa Kanada, 2002: Kanada's team passed one trillion digits, working on a Hitachi supercomputer and checking the result with two different formulas.
The record for digits of π.Fabrice Bellard, 2009: The French programmer behind QEMU and FFmpeg beat supercomputers using a desktop PC and a clever, efficient program.
The record for digits of π.Emma Haruka Iwao, 2019: A Google engineer broke the record using cloud computers, and she celebrated the record on Pi Day.
The record for digits of π.Google Cloud, 2022: This run took about 157 days on cloud machines, and the result needed hundreds of terabytes of storage.
